basis.claim: you can use ORDER BY only at the end of the statement. This restriction applies only to when you specify UNION, EXCEPT, and INTERSECT in a top-level query and not in a subquery. / The ORDER BY clause is not valid in views, inline functions, derived tables, and subqueries, unless either the TOP or OFFSET and FETCH clauses are also specified ... used only to determine the rows returned by the TOP clause

Will Assaf, 2015-06-08: SELECT * FROM ( SELECT TOP 1 * FROM @tbl t ORDER BY t.id DESC UNION ALL SELECT TOP 1 * FROM @tbl t ORDER BY t.id DESC ) x works; without the wrapper it fails with Msg 156 Incorrect syntax near the keyword UNION.

classes.structure_basis: An ORDER BY after a branch with TOP inside a subquery belongs to that branch: attached to the union it would leave a derived table with ORDER BY and no TOP, which the ORDER BY page makes invalid. After a last branch without TOP it stays the union's (with OFFSET/FETCH, as at top level). Top-level set_operation unchanged. OFFSET/FETCH is part of the ORDER BY clause and TOP cannot share a query scope with it, so an ORDER BY followed by OFFSET/FETCH after a last TOP branch is the union's. Review r1 (separate context) agreed for the two-TOP-branch shape, which the SQLServerCentral result confirms; for a TOP branch only last (earlier branch without TOP) the branch attachment is the only reading consistent with the ORDER BY and TOP pages but has no engine observation, and r5 parsed that shape with the union attachment.
classes.change: subquery uses _subquery_query_expression/_subquery_set_operation; _ordered_top_branch (dynamic precedence 1) keeps TOP ... ORDER BY inside the branch query_specification; the union trailing clauses inside a subquery take OFFSET/FETCH only after their own ORDER BY, so an OFFSET without ORDER BY there is now an error (r5 accepted it; the top-level set_operation is unchanged and still accepts it)
